source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Thank you again for these. I really appreciate how systematically you've approached each round. It has made this process so much easier, and I truly feel like we're in the final refinements.

After spending some time with these, I actually realized that I may have unintentionally introduced some ambiguity by using the word "reach." I think what I was trying to communicate was much more mechanical than artistic.

When I asked for more reach on Variation 1, what I was really asking for was a very slight increase in the length of the right arm while leaving the existing Option B terminal completely unchanged. Looking back, I think "length" would have been a much better word than "reach."

Because the terminal itself evolved in Variation 1, I'm finding it difficult to evaluate the one variable I was actually trying to study. I was hoping to compare the original Option B with a version that was identical in every way except for a very subtle increase in the length of the right arm.

For the next round, I'd love to explore it this way:

1\. Starting with the original Option B, increase only the length of the right arm by a very small amount. Please do not change the terminal geometry, taper, point shape, or profile. Imagine simply extending the existing arm slightly farther along the exact same line before it ends. Then apply that identical change to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

The horizontal reference line was incredibly helpful, so I'd love to keep that for this comparison.

2\. Starting from that longer version of Option B, keep the exact same increase in length, but soften the terminal ever so slightly. I'm not looking for additional curvature or a flourish—just a gentler finish while preserving the same architectural character. The tip should remain straight, with only the sharpness of the corners being softened very subtly.

3\. Take Option C and apply that same subtle increase in length while keeping its existing terminal character and overall geometry unchanged. Again, carry that consistently through the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

I actually think Variations 2 and 3 did a nice job exploring the softer terminal language. The only challenge is that they were built from a Variation 1 terminal that had already changed, so it's difficult for me to separate the effect of the increased length from the effect of the redesigned terminal.

At this point, I really feel like we're evaluating one variable at a time. The overall architecture, proportions, slope, spacing, and finish all feel locked. I'm simply trying to determine whether the logo becomes even stronger with a slightly longer right arm before deciding whether that terminal should remain exactly as it is or become just a touch softer.

Thank you again for all of your thoughtful work. We're incredibly close, and I really appreciate your patience in exploring these final nuances.

value_updates.right_arm_length_change: very small increase along the existing line
